historical_record.description: The Art Commission approved the final working drawings for the McLaren Park Swimming Pool, Visitacion Avenue and Hahn Street, designed by William G. Merchant, Architect.
The Art Commission approved the final working drawings for the neighborhood playground and clubhouse at Visitacion Avenue and Hahn Street, designed by Hans U. Gerson.
The Art Commission approved the Phase III plans for the amphitheater in McLaren Park, with a commendation.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to build the McLaren Park swimming pool to Engstrum & Nourse at $352,900.

The Recreation and Park Commission recorded that the last lawsuits and negotiations were cleared and all property within McLaren Park's final boundaries could now be acquired, after decades in which the planned park had been repeatedly cut back, and credited Commissioner Francis J. Herz, its McLaren Park chairman.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved the preliminary drawings, plans and elevation by Vincent G. Raney, architect, for a proposed playground and maintenance yard at University and Wayland Avenues in McLaren Park.

In a set of names its committee had cleared with the Mayor, the Recreation and Park Commission named McLaren Park's new road John F. Shelley Drive, the lake at University and Wayland John L. McNab Lake, and the stables there the Byron Getchell Stables.

The Recreation and Park Commission renamed the McLaren Swimming Pool the William M. Coffman Swimming Pool, for its former vice president and his interest in aquatic sports; the naming ceremony was set for September 23.
The Recreation and Park Commission approved an agreement with J. Francis Ward, architect, to draw plans for developing 13 acres of McLaren Park, at a fee of $13,500.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved J. Francis Ward's preliminary plan for developing the University and Mansell area of McLaren Park, asking for wider paths and the tennis courts set parallel.

The Recreation and Park Commission engaged Yuill-Thornton, Warner & Levikow, Inc. to design and supervise an amphitheater in John McLaren Park, for a fee of $16,500, asking that it seat at least 1,200.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved J. Francis Ward's final plans for developing McLaren Park near Mansell and University Streets, estimated at $153,150, asking for plastic or plexiglass in place of plate glass.
The Recreation and Park Commission approved Yuill-Thornton, Warner and Levikow's final plans for an amphitheater in McLaren Park, estimated at $220,000.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to build the amphitheater in McLaren Park to G. M. Labrucherie and Associates at $226,669.
